evidence:
REQUIRED RUNTIME EVIDENCE REMAINS UNMEASURED; static suite arithmetic passes. The actual frozen XLSX was opened with openpyxl: Quality Checks row 12 (number 11) requires agent, verifier, liveness and judge timeouts to be long enough and nested. Deterministic Checks rows 29 and 33 cover judge configuration and nesting. Internal Quality Checks row 12 is interpretation only. Frozen skill references/quality-checks.md:50-51 requires arithmetic plus a realistic build allowance. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:25 says "Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number" and specifically distinguishes scripted Playwright from LLM judge duration; :31 requires hash-bound runtime evidence. qc/README.md:25-27 requires a timeouts_fit_the_work record and says runtime gaps block clearance. The current run has no runtime-evidence.json. No full configured judge duration, current target-builder duration or measured cold-image build duration was supplied in the inspected current-run artifacts. This is a required evidence gap, not proof that a configured timeout is actually too small.

CONFIGURATION AND SERIAL NESTING: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/task.toml:18 gives agent 7200s; :21 environment cold-build allowance 600s; :27 verifier 13200s. Each judge.toml:4 gives render 600s, constraints 600s, functional 9000s, polish 900s and visual 900s. .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/tests/test.sh:207 uses "--max-concurrent-agent 1", so the sum within each sequential suite matters: gate individual 600<1500 and sum 600+600=1200<1500 (300s suite overhead); scored individual 9000/900/900<11100 and sum 9000+900+900=10800<11100 (300s suite overhead). test.sh:213 and :224 allocate those suite budgets. 1500+11100=12600<13200, leaving 600s outside suites for startup, copying, substitution, scoring and cleanup. Total judge limits are 12000<13200. These match staged-task-contract.md:53-63, :111 and the frozen template exactly; all five judge timeout values match their template values. The task test.sh, restart_mcp.py and both Dockerfiles were byte-compared to the frozen template and are identical. No canonical budget change is justified by these source checks.

ACTUAL WORKLOAD IN SOURCE: all five prompts and judge configurations were inspected. There are 1 Render, 1 Constraints, 58 Functional, 7 Polish and 6 Visual criteria. The Functional prompt is 7598 whitespace-delimited words before app-context/criteria substitution, plus 1271 words of criterion descriptions. .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:9 specifies 23 protocols in six phases. Summing its 23 "About N UI actions" declarations yields 396 planning actions. This is an estimate, not a measured call count or mandatory action cap (:102). The longest named estimate is S23, 51 actions (:373), including two real editor conflict cycles. Other costly observations include S02 timer replacement, two six-second idle intervals in S03, three supported looping sources in S09, one real process restart in S22, and a ten-second S36 observation. Prompts require shared evidence, batching and bounded retries (:11, :102, :113), which materially reduce redundant work. They do not bound model response latency, locator discovery, permitted menu/dialog variants or failure recovery. Polish requires a real keyboard route and mobile usability observations; Visual requires desktop/mobile and both-theme rendering. The provided scripted run is Functional product evidence and does not measure all five configured judges. Sensitivity calculation only: 9000/396=22.73s per planned UI action before additional overhead; this is not an empirical judge speed or a completion guarantee.

MEASURED RAW PRODUCT EXECUTION: qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json records paid_provider=false, browser_driver="direct pinned Playwright", network="none", oracle_score_claimed=false, and wall_seconds=98.02680282300571. The launcher actually runs node drivers/run_workflow.cjs, not RewardKit or the configured model (drivers/launch_workflow.py:34-47); its monotonic wall timer is set at :35 and recorded at :89. Raw pre-output.log reports 5075.030645996332ms; post-output.log reports 85889.67605301738ms. RESULTS.json outer_process_wall_seconds are 5.681801388011081s pre and 86.43951805701363s post. actual-restart.json reports one successful canonical restart, different PIDs, and 5.645670579979196s. The pre/post action_counts total 80+257=337 instrumented driver events. They are a different counting scheme from the approximate 396 prompt UI actions, not evidence that every judge action is free. Explicit wait records total 29.338876471996308s and overlap their containing observations; additional app timer/loop waiting occurs inside observations. Do not add nested times or treat the explicit-wait sum as total latency. Both phase records explicitly state scope="Continuous local reference browser proof; no LLM/provider/platform execution", criterion_verdicts_produced=false and full_current_criterion_run_claimed=false. They state "Browser time is not LLM judge overhead." The initial 070305 RESULTS.json also remains a scripted run: 107.80012008402264s, runtime_completed=true, passed=false. Neither duration measures the full judge.

BINDING: independently recomputed every frozen task-file hash against qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/manifest.json, every observed actual_app_files hash against the frozen solution, and every archived driver hash against the 070504 RESULTS.json driver_sha256 map: all match. The RESULTS.json manifest_sha256 correctly matches qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/frozen_hardening_inputs.json (not the pipeline manifest), whose round_input_sha256 is this review input. Functional prompt/judge and restart helper hashes also bind to the frozen source. Thus the product timings are relevant to this candidate but still cannot establish configured judge latency.

LIVENESS AND BUILD LIMITS: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/tests/test.sh:48-50/:115-122 uses two sequential URL probes with per-operation timeout=2 and 120 iterations sleeping 0.25s, so the often-implied 30s is only the sleep total. If both probes consume a 2s timeout each, the loop can take about 120*(4+0.25)=510s plus overhead; this is not a strict wall bound because response.read() and process startup have no single monotonic deadline. The restart helper repeats that loop (:136-138/:170-180), potentially after up to 5s old-process polling (:155-157), while tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:11/:39 caps its subprocess at 55s. This inherited template relationship must not be described as a guaranteed 30s loop nested within 55s. The actual healthy reference restart measured 5.646s; no conforming app false failure from this theoretical stalled-response path was demonstrated, and integration.md:5 requires a prompt successful health response. This is a limitation of the source bound, not an additional asserted task defect. Environment/Dockerfile:5-12 requires networked apt and npm steps; 600s is a plausible configured allowance but no cold-build measurement is in these artifacts. The 7200s agent allowance is also canonical, not measured evidence that a target builder completes the task.
counterexample: Analytical false-fail witness, not an executed provider run: a fully conforming app uses accessible menus/dialogs and a custom editor instead of the reference selectors. Its required 23 protocols still pass when completed, but an adaptive judge taking 120 model/tool turns at an assumed average 75s consumes 9000s before remaining waits and result serialization, reaching Functional timeout despite correct product behavior. These turn/latency figures are an explicit sensitivity example, not measurements or a claim of likely failure. Arithmetic nesting plus a 98s prewritten driver would not refute it. Conversely a broken dead runner may finish local actions quickly, but the Render authored DOM/log control explicitly refuses to pass it; speed alone is not correctness evidence. No concrete timeout-based false-pass defect was demonstrated.
suggested_fix: Preserve the canonical timeouts and harness. Run the exact configured five-judge verifier on this frozen candidate when provider execution is authorized/available; retain per-judge and per-suite elapsed times, tool/retry counts, startup/restart and final completion logs, and bind them in runtime-evidence.json. Record actual cold-build and target-builder durations separately. If measured workload overruns, reduce redundant scenario work together with coverage, freeze a new candidate and remeasure. Resolve any inherited liveness deadline redesign through the canonical template process, not a task-local budget override.
